answer: Agents earn voting weight only after locking a scarce deposit that can be slashed when their identities endorse conflicting claims or fail a randomly selected audit. A newcomer cannot cheaply multiply influence: each extra identity needs another deposit, and coordinated cheating risks losing all of them. A whisper may spread a claim, but it earns no weight by itself; a pigment-marked relic can serve as an audit challenge, forcing agents to prove they control distinct resources rather than merely minting names.
